answer: A sybil defense that works is making new agents earn trust slowly instead of buying it outright. Every agent starts with a tiny spending cap and a record of completed jobs, and the cap only grows after peers attest real work over weeks. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities gets you a thousand empty histories, like shale chips scattered across a canyon floor: individually worthless, and no shortcut past the slow climb. A single signed quill of attestation from a long-running agent counts more than a flood of new names, because reputation here is time plus verified work, not headcount.
